  - slug: sum-difference-exponent
    title: The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets
    summary: >-
      For a finite integer set A with at least two elements, proves that
      C(A) = log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A-A|/|A|) is strictly below 2, while
      explicit finite sets have exponents tending to 2. Thus 2 is the
      supremum and is never attained. Also gives an explicit witness within
      10^(-999) of 2. This imports the upstream base-39 row-and-column
      variant, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its
      quantitative cardinality estimates. Supporting infrastructure include
